cards.title: Correspondent banking under the Directions
The offshore request
cards.setting: Financial institutions desk, Connaught Place. 11:30 am.

lines.text: The respondent, Halcyon Trust Bank, is licensed in a small island jurisdiction. Its 'head office' is a registered agent's address. No staff, no management on the island.
But the relationship manager says it would bring in large USD deposits from a regulated group.
Is it part of a regulated financial group under effective consolidated supervision? He couldn't tell me.
Then we need a decision rule before Monday's audit.

cards.title: Halcyon Trust Bank
cards.situation: Halcyon is incorporated and licensed offshore, has no meaningful management or staff there, and its relationship manager cannot show it belongs to any regulated group under consolidated supervision. It asks for a USD vostro account and payable-through access for its own clients.

choices.text: Decline: on these facts Halcyon meets the definition of a shell bank, and the Directions forbid correspondent relationships with shell banks.
choices.outcome: Correct. A bank with no physical presence (meaningful mind and management) where it is licensed, and no affiliation with a supervised regulated group, is a shell bank. No approval can cure that.

choices.text: Proceed if senior management approves now and the Board ratifies it later.
choices.outcome: The approval route applies to permitted relationships. It cannot authorise a relationship with a shell bank.

choices.text: Open the vostro account but refuse payable-through access.
choices.outcome: Limiting the product does not change who the respondent is. Any correspondent relationship with a shell bank is prohibited.

choices.text: Ask for more evidence of group membership and physical presence before deciding, and do not open anything meanwhile.
choices.outcome: Reasonable while facts are unclear, but if the evidence does not appear, the answer must be a clear decline and the file should record why.

The ML/TF risk assessment was last reviewed 20 months ago

cards.title: Kaveri Meridian's AML/CFT programme cycle
cards.caption: Paragraphs 10-12, 72 and 79 of the KYC Directions. The audit function itself must be staffed with people well trained in KYC/AML/CFT.

items.label: Risk assessment
items.detail: Documented, proportionate, reviewed at least annually and presented to the Board.

items.label: Policy and controls
items.detail: Board-approved KYC policy and a risk-based approach, including for new products.

items.label: People
items.detail: Know Your Employee screening and ongoing training tailored to each role.

items.label: Operate
items.detail: CDD, monitoring, screening and prompt reporting to FIU-IND.

items.label: Assure
items.detail: Independent evaluation, concurrent and internal audit, quarterly notes to the Audit Committee.

cards.front: How often is the ML/TF risk assessment reviewed?
cards.back: At least annually, at a periodicity the Board or its committee sets; the outcome goes to the Board and is available to competent authorities.

cards.front: When must a new product be risk-assessed?
cards.back: Before it is launched or used, with a risk-based approach to manage what the assessment finds.
Staff through an ongoing programme on the KYC/AML/CFT policy, focused differently for frontline, compliance and onboarding staff; audit staff must be well versed too.
A screening mechanism built into recruitment, so that staff handling KYC/AML/CFT have integrity and sound knowledge.

cards.front: Can the bank deal with FATF-listed countries?
cards.back: Yes, legitimate trade can continue, but with effective, proportionate EDD and written findings kept for RBI.
FIU-IND under PMLA section 13 for reporting-entity failures; RBI under the Banking Regulation Act for breaches of its Directions.

Not execute the wire transfer
Execute it if the amount is below ₹5 lakh
Execute it and file a CTR for the month
cards.explanation: Paragraph 74 says the ordering bank shall not execute the wire transfer if it cannot comply with the information requirements. The three-working-day window is only for small domestic transfers by non-account holders.

cards.title: Stage five take-aways
items: Check the UNSC, 2007 Order and UNSCR 1718 lists daily; never hold accounts for listed persons; report resembling accounts to FIU-IND and advise MHA under the 2021 UAPA Order.
Under WMD Act section 12A, do not transact with designated persons, inform the Director, FIU-IND (the CNO) immediately and copy the State Nodal Officer and RBI.
Cross-border wires must carry full originator and beneficiary data; an ordering bank that cannot comply must not send the transfer.
Correspondent banking needs respondent due diligence, prior senior management and post facto Board approval, documented responsibilities and no shell banks.
The programme rests on an annual ML/TF risk assessment, a Board-approved KYC policy, independent audit with quarterly notes, and ongoing role-based training.

quiz.question: Under paragraph 56 of the KYC Directions, which UN lists must banks check for UAPA section 51A purposes?
options: Only the OFAC SDN list published in the United States
Only lists published by the Indian Banks' Association
The ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions List and the Taliban Sanctions List
The FATF grey list and the FATF black list
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 56 names the UNSC ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida list and the Taliban list, plus the schedules to the 2007 Order. OFAC and FATF statements are different instruments.

quiz.question: A customer's name matches an entry on the designated list under section 12A of the WMD Act. Whom must the bank inform immediately?
options: The local police station, with a copy to the customer
The Central Nodal Officer, i.e. the Director, FIU-IND, with copies to the State Nodal Officer and RBI
The Ministry of External Affairs only
Its correspondent bank abroad, which handles the freeze
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 57 requires immediate information with full particulars to the CNO (Director, FIU-IND), with a copy to the State Nodal Officer and RBI.

quiz.question: The sanctions team updated the screening lists last on Monday. It is now Thursday and a new UN listing was published on Tuesday. What is the issue?
options: No issue, because weekly updates are acceptable
No issue, because UN listings take effect only after RBI circulates them
The only issue is that MHA must be told of the delay
The Directions require the lists to be verified daily, so Tuesday's change should already be in use
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 56 requires daily verification of the lists, taking additions, deletions and changes into account for meticulous compliance.

quiz.question: A non-account holder asks the bank to send ₹60,000 by NEFT to a supplier in Jaipur. What information must accompany the transfer?
options: Full originator and beneficiary information, as for a cross-border transfer
Only a unique transaction reference number
Only the beneficiary's account number and IFSC
No information, because domestic transfers are exempt
quiz.explanation: Domestic wire transfers of ₹50,000 and above where the originator is not an account holder must carry the same originator and beneficiary information as cross-border transfers.

quiz.question: Which approval is required to establish a new cross-border correspondent banking relationship?
options: Prior approval from RBI's Foreign Exchange Department
Prior approval from senior management, followed by post facto approval of the Board or empowered committee
Approval of the Principal Officer only
Post facto approval of the Audit Committee only
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 73 requires prior senior management approval and post facto approval from the Board or the empowered committee.

quiz.question: Under the KYC Directions, what is a shell bank?
options: A bank with no physical presence where it is licensed and no affiliation with a supervised regulated group
Any bank incorporated in an offshore financial centre
A bank that offers only correspondent and trade services
Any bank that has been fined for AML failures
quiz.explanation: A shell bank lacks meaningful mind and management in its country of incorporation and licensing and is unaffiliated with a regulated group under effective consolidated supervision.

quiz.question: How often, at a minimum, must the bank review its ML/TF risk assessment?
options: At least every six months
At least annually
At least every three years
Only after an RBI inspection
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10 lets the Board set the periodicity in line with the assessment's outcome, but the bank must review it at least annually.

quiz.question: Kaveri Meridian plans to launch a new prepaid instant-payment product next month. What do the Directions require first?
options: FIU-IND registration of the product before launch
An ML/TF risk assessment before the product is launched, and risk-based controls to manage the risks found
A risk assessment within six months after the launch
Approval from the Indian Banks' Association
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 72 requires ML/TF risk assessments before launching new products, practices or technologies, and a risk-based approach to managing the risks.

quiz.question: A beneficiary bank keeps receiving cross-border transfers from one ordering bank with the originator information missing. What should it have?
options: A rule to credit all such transfers and ignore the gaps
A rule to return all such transfers without review
A rule to report all such transfers in the monthly CTR
Risk-based policies to decide when to execute, reject or suspend such transfers and what follow-up to take
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 74 requires beneficiary banks to identify transfers lacking required information and to have risk-based policies on executing, rejecting or suspending them, including follow-up and STRs where suspicious.

quiz.question: Which statement about transactions with countries named in FATF statements is correct under the Directions?
options: Legitimate trade may continue, but with effective, proportionate EDD and written findings kept for RBI
All transactions with such countries are prohibited
No extra measures are needed unless RBI names the customer
Only transactions above ₹10 lakh need any review
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 61 requires EDD proportionate to the risk, examination of background and purpose, and retained written findings, while not precluding legitimate trade.

options: The Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025
The FIU-IND reporting format guide
The Prevention of Money-laundering Act, 2002 on its own
The Indian Banks' Association KYC guidance notes
bank.explanation: On 28 November 2025 RBI issued entity-wise Directions; commercial banks now follow the KYC Directions 2025. The PMLA sets the legal duties, FIU-IND's guide covers report formats, and IBA notes may inform risk assessment but are not RBI's instructions.

bank.question: The Director, FIU-IND finds that Kaveri Meridian's Designated Director failed to ensure that a reporting procedure was followed. Which statement about the Director's powers is correct?
options: The Director may penalise only the bank, never an individual
The Director may imprison the Designated Director for up to three years
The Director may impose a penalty on the Designated Director personally, of ₹10,000 to ₹1 lakh for each failure
The Director must refer the matter to RBI, which alone can act
bank.explanation: Section 13(2) lets the Director warn, direct, require reports or fine the reporting entity, its designated director on the Board or any employee, between ₹10,000 and ₹1 lakh per failure. Imprisonment relates to the money-laundering offence under section 4.

bank.question: Kaveri Meridian is restructuring. Which proposal complies with the KYC Directions?
options: The Principal Officer also becomes Designated Director to simplify reporting lines
An independent non-executive director is named Designated Director
The Designated Director role is left vacant while a search takes place
The Board names a whole-time director as Designated Director and a separate management-level officer as Principal Officer
bank.explanation: The Designated Director must be the Managing Director or a whole-time director authorised by the Board, and the Principal Officer cannot be nominated as Designated Director. Both must be in place and notified to FIU-IND and RBI.

bank.question: Which pair of statements correctly describes the punishment for the offence of money laundering under section 4 of the PMLA?
options: Simple imprisonment of up to two years, or a fine, at the court's choice
Rigorous imprisonment of at least three years and up to seven years, plus a fine; a higher cap of ten years applies for certain scheduled offences
A fine of ₹10,000 to ₹1 lakh for each failure, imposed by FIU-IND
Rigorous imprisonment of up to three years, with no minimum term
bank.explanation: Section 4 provides rigorous imprisonment of three to seven years and a fine, rising to ten years for offences in paragraph 2 of Part A of the Schedule. The ₹10,000 to ₹1 lakh range is the section 13 administrative penalty.

bank.question: Kaveri Meridian's training plan gives every employee the same 30-minute AML video once a year. Measured against paragraph 79 of the KYC Directions, what is the main gap?
options: The video must be approved by FIU-IND before use
Training must be delivered in person, not by video
Training must be ongoing and focused differently for frontline, compliance and onboarding staff, with special front-desk training
Training is required only every three years, so the plan is excessive
bank.explanation: Paragraph 79 requires an ongoing programme on the KYC/AML/CFT policy with a different focus for frontline staff, compliance staff and staff dealing with new customers, plus special training for front-desk staff on customer-education issues.

bank.question: An internal auditor at Kaveri Meridian is assigned to review KYC/AML compliance but has never been trained on the bank's KYC policy. Which part of the Directions does this conflict with?
options: The requirement that the audit function be staffed with persons adequately trained and well versed in KYC/AML/CFT
The requirement that auditors be approved by FIU-IND
The requirement that the Principal Officer audit his own work
None, because training duties cover only frontline staff
bank.explanation: Paragraph 79(3) requires banks to ensure the audit function is properly staffed with people adequately trained in the bank's KYC/AML/CFT policies, the regulation and related issues.

bank.question: Kaveri Meridian's Singapore branch finds that a Singapore rule prevents it from applying one RBI KYC requirement. What must the bank do?
options: Bring it to RBI's notice; RBI may advise further action, including extra measures to manage ML/TF risk
Ignore the RBI requirement, since host law prevails abroad
Apply the RBI requirement anyway, even if it breaks Singapore law
Close the Singapore branch within three months
bank.explanation: Paragraph 4 says that where host-country law prohibits implementing the Directions, the bank must inform RBI, which may advise further action including additional measures.

bank.question: Which list correctly names the steps paragraph 12 of the KYC Directions uses to ensure compliance with the KYC policy?
options: Annual FIU-IND certification, RBI pre-approval of the policy, and monthly Board reports
External audit by a CERT-In auditor, weekly Board reports, and staff rotation
Customer satisfaction surveys, mystery shopping and branch rankings
Define senior management for KYC, allocate responsibility, independent evaluation, concurrent or internal audit, and quarterly audit notes to the Audit Committee
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12 lists specifying senior management for KYC, allocating responsibility, independent evaluation of compliance functions, concurrent or internal audit, and quarterly audit notes and compliance to the Audit Committee.

bank.question: A reporting entity disagrees with a penalty order made by the Director, FIU-IND under section 13. Where can it appeal?
options: To the RBI Ombudsman
To the Appellate Tribunal under the PMLA
To the Banking Codes and Standards Board
To the Central KYC Records Registry
bank.explanation: Section 26 of the PMLA allows a reporting entity aggrieved by an order of the Director under section 13(2) to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal.

bank.question: A walk-in customer buys drafts of ₹30,000 on Monday and ₹30,000 on Wednesday for the same supplier, saying both are 'part of one order'. What is the correct view?
options: Each draft is under ₹50,000, so no identification is needed
Identification is needed only if he pays in cash
The transactions appear connected and total ₹60,000, so he must be identified
Only a CTR is needed, as the total exceeds ₹50,000
bank.explanation: Paragraph 21 counts several transactions that appear connected. Together they reach ₹50,000 or more, so CIP applies. CTRs relate to cash over ₹10 lakh, not to this threshold.

bank.question: An unincorporated association of traders has no member with more than 15% of its property, capital or profits. Whom must the bank treat as beneficial owner?
options: The natural person who holds the position of senior managing official
Every member with more than 5%
The association itself, as a body of individuals
Nobody, so beneficial owner identification is waived
bank.explanation: Where no natural person meets the ownership test for a company, partnership or association, the beneficial owner is the relevant natural person who is the senior managing official.

bank.question: A company customer is listed on the National Stock Exchange of India. What does paragraph 38 say about identifying its shareholders and beneficial owners?
options: All shareholders above 10% must still be identified
It is not necessary to identify and verify any shareholder or beneficial owner of such a listed entity
The bank must obtain SEBI's list of beneficial owners
Only the promoter group must be identified and verified
bank.explanation: Paragraph 38 exempts entities listed on a stock exchange in India, entities listed in notified jurisdictions, and subsidiaries of such listed entities from shareholder and beneficial owner identification.

bank.question: A customer with a valid KYC Identifier wants an account. The CKYCR record shows an old address, and she says she has moved. What should the bank do?
options: Reject the KYC Identifier and restart full CDD from paper documents
Open the account with the old address and update it at periodic updation
Use the CKYCR record but obtain updated address information, since her information has changed
Ask her to update CKYCR herself before the bank can proceed
bank.explanation: The bank should retrieve records with the KYC Identifier and may seek further documents only in listed cases, such as when the customer's information has changed. It then updates CKYCR with the new information.

bank.question: An existing KYC-compliant savings customer wants to open a current account for her sole proprietorship. What CDD is required?
options: Full fresh CDD of her as an individual, as for a new customer
Nothing at all, because she already has an account
Only a self-declaration that the business is genuine
No fresh identification of her as an individual, but the bank obtains the required proofs of the proprietorship's business activity
bank.explanation: CDD applies at UCIC level, so she need not be re-identified. For a sole proprietorship, the Directions also require documents proving the firm's business or activity (normally two, one in exceptional cases).

bank.question: Which of the following conditions is NOT required for Kaveri Meridian to rely on CDD done by a third party?
options: The bank obtains the CDD records immediately from the third party or CKYCR
The third party must be based in India
The third party is regulated and has CDD and record-keeping measures
The third party is not in a country assessed as high-risk
bank.explanation: Paragraph 22 requires immediate access to records, assurance of copies on request, a regulated third party, and that it is not based in a high-risk country. There is no requirement that it be in India; the bank keeps ultimate responsibility.

bank.question: A branch rejects an elderly applicant with a disability because 'the paperwork looks like trouble', without reviewing her documents. What do the Directions say?
options: The branch has full discretion and need not give reasons
The bank must not reject without applying its mind, the officer must record the reasons, and the policy must not deny access to disadvantaged people
Rejection is fine if the branch files an STR afterwards
Only the Principal Officer may reject applications
bank.explanation: Paragraph 18 says the Customer Acceptance Policy must not deny banking to the public, especially the disadvantaged including persons with disabilities, and rejections need application of mind with reasons recorded.

bank.question: Mr Joshi pays ₹49,000 in cash on three consecutive days to buy prepaid travel cards at a branch where he has no account, each time asking whether the amount is 'below the limit'. What should the bank do?
options: Nothing, since each transaction is below ₹50,000
Refuse the third payment but keep no record
Identify him, as the bank has reason to believe he is structuring below ₹50,000, and consider an STR
Identify him only if the total exceeds ₹10 lakh
bank.explanation: Paragraph 21 requires identification where the bank believes a customer is intentionally structuring transactions below ₹50,000. The pattern and his questions also justify considering an STR.

bank.question: In March 2026 RBI penalised Central Bank of India ₹63.60 lakh. Which KYC failing was among the sustained charges?
options: Failing to obtain introductions for new accounts
Failing to file cross-border wire transfer reports
Failing to upload certain customers' KYC records to CKYCR within the prescribed timeline
Failing to screen customers against the UNSCR 1718 list
bank.explanation: RBI's press release lists failure to upload KYC records to CKYCR within the timeline and opening additional BSBD accounts for customers who already had one.

bank.question: During V-CIP, the customer's Aadhaar Secure QR code was generated five working days before the call. What should the official do?
options: Accept it, as Aadhaar data does not expire
Accept it if a supervisor countersigns
Accept it and verify the address later by letter
Not accept it, because the QR code or XML file must not be older than three working days on the day of V-CIP
bank.explanation: Paragraph 27(2)(viii) requires the XML file or Secure QR code to be no older than three working days from the date of the V-CIP.

bank.question: Kaveri Meridian's V-CIP vendor proposes hosting the video platform on its own servers and keeping copies of recordings for 'analytics'. Which requirement does this break?
options: None, provided the vendor is located in India
Only the rule on geo-tagging of recordings
The bank must house V-CIP infrastructure on its premises and, if using cloud, ensure all data goes to the bank and the provider keeps none
Only the requirement for a CERT-In empanelled auditor
bank.explanation: Paragraph 27(1)(i) requires the infrastructure in the bank's own premises and connections from its secured network; in a cloud model the bank owns the data, recordings move to its servers immediately and the provider retains no data.

bank.question: A V-CIP account was opened correctly on Friday. When can the customer start transacting?
options: Only after the account has been subjected to concurrent audit
Immediately after the call ends
After the first credit from another bank account
After 30 days of monitoring as a high-risk account
bank.explanation: Paragraph 27(2)(xv) says accounts opened through V-CIP become operational only after concurrent audit. The first-credit rule applies to non-face-to-face accounts not opened through V-CIP.

bank.question: Ms Kaur opened an account non-face-to-face using an equivalent e-document, not V-CIP or Aadhaar OTP e-KYC. Her first transaction request is a cash deposit at an ATM. What applies?
options: Any credit is acceptable as the first transaction
Only her first withdrawal is restricted
No restriction applies once PAN is verified
The first transaction must be a credit from her existing KYC-compliant bank account, so the cash deposit cannot be the first transaction
bank.explanation: Paragraph 44(5) requires the first transaction in such accounts to be a credit from the customer's existing KYC-complied bank account. The account is also high-risk until verified face to face or by V-CIP.

bank.question: A long-standing customer is a senior official of a state-owned enterprise in India (not a foreign one). Under the KYC Directions' PEP paragraph, which statement is correct?
options: He is automatically a PEP and needs senior management approval
He is not a PEP under the Directions' definition, but the bank's own policy and risk assessment still decide how he is treated
He must be exited, as domestic officials cannot hold accounts
He is a PEP only if his account balance exceeds ₹10 lakh
bank.explanation: The Directions define PEPs as those entrusted with prominent public functions by a foreign country. A domestic official is outside that definition, though the bank may treat him as higher risk under its own policy.

bank.question: Kaveri Meridian's medium-risk customer last updated KYC in January 2020. What is the latest periodic updation date under the minimum periods in the Directions?
options: January 2022
January 2025
January 2030
January 2028
bank.explanation: Periodic updation is required at least once every eight years for medium-risk customers, counted from account opening or the last updation: January 2020 plus eight years is January 2028.

bank.question: A legal entity customer confirms at periodic updation that its directors and shareholding have changed. What must the bank do?
options: Carry out the KYC process equivalent to onboarding a new legal entity customer
Accept a self-declaration through the registered email
Record the change at the next periodic updation
Update only the beneficial owner names in its system
bank.explanation: Paragraph 42(4) requires, where an LE's KYC information has changed, the KYC process applicable to onboarding a new LE customer. A self-declaration suffices only where nothing has changed.

bank.question: A customer whose account was opened when he was a minor turns 18. What do the Directions require?
options: Nothing until his next periodic updation
Closing the minor account and opening a new one through V-CIP only
Fresh photographs and ensuring CDD documents meet current standards, with fresh KYC where needed
A letter of consent from his guardian
bank.explanation: Paragraph 42(3)(v) requires fresh photographs when the customer becomes a major and that CDD documents meet current standards; fresh KYC may be done where required.

bank.question: Which transaction pattern do the Directions say must be immediately reported to RBI and other authorities such as FIU-IND?
options: A salaried customer receiving a bonus credit
A retailer depositing daily cash takings at one branch
A customer paying an insurance premium by cheque
A company seeking a large number of cheque books, with many small cash deposits across the country into one account
bank.explanation: The explanation under paragraph 41, on marketing and MLM firms, requires such cases (many cheque books, multiple small cash deposits nationwide, or many cheques of similar amounts and dates) to be reported immediately to RBI and other authorities such as FIU-IND.

bank.question: A charitable trust registered as an NPO receives a single donation of ₹12 lakh by bank transfer. What reporting duty arises for the bank?
options: A CTR, because the amount exceeds ₹10 lakh
An STR, because all NPO receipts are suspicious
No report, because the transfer was not in cash
The receipt goes in the monthly report on NPO transactions, due by the 15th of the next month
bank.explanation: Rule 3(1)(BA) covers receipts by non-profit organisations of more than ₹10 lakh, reported monthly by the 15th under Rule 8(1). CTRs are for cash, and an STR needs actual suspicion.

bank.question: A customer pays in ₹40,000 in cash, and the teller finds that two ₹500 notes are counterfeit. What reporting duty arises under Rule 3?
options: None, because the amount is below ₹10 lakh
Only an internal incident report is needed
The transaction is reportable as one where counterfeit currency notes were used as genuine
Only a CTR at month end
bank.explanation: Rule 3(1)(C) covers all cash transactions where forged or counterfeit notes have been used as genuine, regardless of the ₹10 lakh threshold; they are reported monthly by the 15th.

bank.question: Arjun closes 300 alerts in one day with the note 'activity normal'. Six months later FIU-IND finds STRs should have been filed on several. Based on the Union Bank of India order, which failings are likely to be found?
options: Failure to report STRs and to maintain an effective internal mechanism to detect and report suspicious transactions
Only a failure to file CTRs
Only a breach of the KYC Identifier rule
No failing, because alerts are internal documents
bank.explanation: In the 2024 Union Bank order, FIU-IND found failures to report suspicious transactions and to evolve an internal mechanism for detecting and reporting them, along with ongoing due diligence failures, after alerts were closed with minimal justification.

bank.question: Which statement about the confidentiality of reports to FIU-IND is correct?
options: Only the Principal Officer is bound by confidentiality
Confidentiality ends once FIU-IND acknowledges the report
The customer may be told if he asks in writing
The bank, its directors, officers and all employees must keep the fact of reporting confidential, though group-wide sharing of unusual-activity analysis is allowed with safeguards
bank.explanation: Rule 8(6) and paragraph 54 bind the bank, its directors, officers and all employees. Sharing analysis of unusual transactions under group-wide policies is permitted, with safeguards against tipping off.

bank.question: A relationship manager learns an STR was filed on his client. He emails the client: 'Compliance is looking at your transfers; keep them small for a while.' What is wrong?
options: He has tipped off the client and breached the duty to keep reporting confidential
Nothing, because he did not mention FIU-IND by name
Only that he used email instead of a phone call
Only that he should have copied the Principal Officer
bank.explanation: Disclosing that the client is under review and coaching him to change behaviour breaches the confidentiality duty and is tipping off, whether or not FIU-IND is named. Coaching smaller transfers also encourages structuring.

bank.question: Which information must a bank's transaction record contain so that an individual transaction can be reconstructed?
options: The nature, the amount and currency, the date, and the parties to the transaction
The customer's risk category and the reasons for it
The branch manager's approval and the teller's ID only
The customer's PAN and CKYCR identifier only
bank.explanation: Rule 4 and paragraph 50 require the nature of the transaction, its amount and currency, its date and the parties to it.

bank.question: Kaveri Meridian filed a CTR on 15 May but later found one transaction was misreported. It corrected the report on 25 May. How does Rule 8 view this?
options: Corrections have no deadline, so there is no issue
Each day of delay in correcting a misreported transaction beyond the time limit is a separate violation
Only the original report date matters
A correction within one month is always allowed
bank.explanation: Rule 8(4) and paragraph 54 treat each day of delay in reporting or in rectifying a misreported transaction beyond the time limit as a separate violation.

bank.question: Through which FIU-IND system do reporting entities register and file their reports?
options: FINnet 2.0, using the FINGate 2.0 portal
CKYCR, operated by CERSAI
The RBI Reporting Portal (CIMS)
The Income Tax e-filing portal
bank.explanation: FIU-IND's site lists reporting-entity registration on FINnet 2.0 and report filing on FINGate 2.0. CKYCR stores KYC records; it is not used for STRs or CTRs.

bank.question: Which description of a 'suspicious transaction' in the KYC Directions is correct?
options: Any transaction, including an attempted one, that gives reasonable grounds to suspect proceeds of a scheduled offence regardless of value, or appears unusually complex, without economic rationale, or linked to terrorism
Any cash transaction above ₹10 lakh, or a series of connected ones in a month
Any transaction by a high-risk customer that exceeds its expected monthly turnover
Only completed transactions that the bank can prove involve criminal proceeds
bank.explanation: The definition covers attempted transactions, cash or not, regardless of value, on four grounds: proceeds of crime, unusual complexity, no economic rationale, or terrorist financing. No proof is needed, only reasonable grounds.

bank.question: A screening match against the UAPA lists turns out to resemble an existing customer closely. Under paragraph 56, whom must the bank inform?
options: Only RBI's Department of Supervision
Only the customer, to give him a chance to explain
FIU-IND, and it must also advise the Ministry of Home Affairs as the 2021 UAPA Order requires
Only the State police, under the CrPC
bank.explanation: Paragraph 56(3) requires the bank to report accounts resembling listed individuals or entities to FIU-IND and to advise MHA under the 2 February 2021 Order.

bank.question: The bank has reasons to believe beyond doubt that a customer's funds fall within section 12A(2)(a) or (b) of the WMD Act, though no freezing order has arrived. What must it do?
options: Wait for the CNO's freezing order before taking any action
Prevent the customer from conducting financial transactions and inform the CNO without delay by email, fax and post
Close the account and pay out the balance by cheque
File an STR only and allow transactions to continue
bank.explanation: Paragraph 57(7) requires the bank to prevent such a person from conducting financial transactions, under intimation to the CNO by email, fax and post, without delay.

bank.question: A customer whose assets were frozen under section 12A of the WMD Act applies to the bank for unfreezing. What must the bank do?
options: Forward the application with full details of the frozen assets to the CNO within two working days
Decide the application itself within 30 days
Unfreeze the assets if the customer provides an indemnity
Send the application to RBI only
bank.explanation: Paragraph 57(9) requires the bank to forward the unfreezing application, with full asset details, to the CNO by email, fax and post within two working days.

bank.question: A walk-in, non-account customer sends ₹20,000 to a relative in Chennai by NEFT. What must the ordering bank include with the transfer?
options: Full originator information including address, as for any cross-border transfer
Nothing, since transfers below ₹50,000 are exempt from all rules
Only the beneficiary's mobile number
At least a unique transaction reference number, provided full details can be made available within three working days on request
bank.explanation: For domestic transfers below ₹50,000 by non-account holders, a unique reference number that allows tracing is enough, as long as the ordering bank can supply the information within three working days of a request.

bank.question: An intermediary bank receives a cross-border transfer whose originator data cannot technically be carried into the related domestic leg. What must it do?
options: Drop the originator data, since the domestic leg is exempt
Return the transfer to the ordering bank in every case
Ask the beneficiary to supply the originator data
Keep a record of all information received for at least five years
bank.explanation: Paragraph 74(2)(ii)(b) requires the intermediary bank to keep a record of all the information received for at least five years where technical limits prevent it travelling with the domestic transfer.

bank.question: Kaveri Meridian controls both the ordering and beneficiary sides of a remittance through its money transfer arrangement. The sending side looks normal but the receiving side shows the beneficiary collecting from 20 unrelated senders. What do the Directions require?
options: Assess each side separately and ignore the other side's data
Consider information from both sides in deciding whether to file an STR, and file one if suspicious
Report only through the monthly cross-border wire report
Ask the ordering customer to explain the beneficiary's activity
bank.explanation: Paragraph 74(2)(iv) requires a bank controlling both sides to take into account all information from both sides when deciding on an STR, and to file one if the transaction is found suspicious.

bank.question: A respondent bank asks Kaveri Meridian for a payable-through account so that its own customers can transact directly. What must Kaveri Meridian be satisfied of?
options: That the respondent's customers have each opened accounts at Kaveri Meridian
That the respondent has done CDD on customers with direct access and monitors them, and can give CDD information immediately on request
That RBI has pre-approved each of the respondent's customers
That the respondent's customers are all resident in India
bank.explanation: Paragraph 73(5)-(6) requires the correspondent to be satisfied that the respondent has conducted CDD and ongoing due diligence on customers with direct access and can provide relevant CDD information immediately on request.

bank.question: Which statement about the bank's ML/TF risk assessment is correct under paragraph 10?
options: It is prepared by FIU-IND and shared with each bank every year
It must be documented, proportionate, reviewed at least annually, presented to the Board or its committee, and made available to competent authorities
It need only cover customers, not products or delivery channels
It is confidential and may not be shown to any authority
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10 requires a documented, proportionate assessment covering clients, countries, products, services, transactions and channels, reviewed at least annually, reported to the Board and available to competent authorities.

bank.question: In June 2026 RBI penalised The Karnal Central Cooperative Bank. Which two KYC failings did RBI find sustained?
options: No Designated Director, and late CTR filing
No V-CIP workflow, and failure to verify GST numbers
No system of periodic review of risk categorisation, and no robust software to identify and report suspicious transactions
No correspondent banking policy, and missing wire transfer data
bank.explanation: RBI's press release on the order of 3 June 2026 lists failure to put in place a system of periodic review of risk categorisation and failure to put in place robust software for identifying and reporting suspicious transactions.
